knowledge:
- key_parameters: TRonly=Logical indicating whether to analyze target regions only (TRUE) or the whole genome (FALSE) ;; threshold1=First coverage depth threshold (e.g., 20) ;; threshold2=Second coverage depth threshold (e.g., 100) ;; percentage1=First percentage threshold of samples (e.g., 0.80) ;; percentage2=Second percentage threshold of samples (e.g., 0.90) ;; mart=A biomaRt object for gene annotation (defaults to hg19 if empty string is provided)
- alternatives: BEDtools or the bamsignals R package can be used for fast coverage calculation of single BAM files or specific windows, but BadRegionFinder is preferred when combining coverage across multiple samples to identify systematically poorly covered regions.
- when_to_use: Use this package when designing or evaluating targeted sequencing experiments (e.g., gene panels) to identify regions or genes that consistently show poor coverage across multiple samples, or to detect high off-target coverage indicating primer design or alignment issues.
- pitfalls: Do not use determineCoverage with TRonly = TRUE if you plan to later select off-target regions using determineRegionsOfInterest, as off-target coverage information is not saved when TRonly = TRUE. Additionally, running determineCoverage with TRonly = FALSE on whole-genome data with many scattered reads can be highly time-consuming.

workflows.name: coverage_quality_analysis
workflows.intent: Determine, classify, and report genomic coverage quality across multiple samples, map bad regions to genes, and visualize the results.
input: SampleNames2.txt (Data frame containing sample names without .bam suffix)
targetRegions2.bed (Data frame or BED file containing target regions with chromosome, start, and end)
BAM/BAI files (Folder containing BAM and corresponding BAI files matching the sample names)
regionsOfInterest (Optional data frame containing specific regions of interest to filter)
workflows.stages: 1. Determine coverage across samples using determineCoverage ;; 2. Classify coverage quality using determineCoverageQuality ;; 3. Filter for regions of interest using determineRegionsOfInterest ;; 4. Retrieve gene annotations and report bad regions using reportBadRegionsSummary, reportBadRegionsDetailed, and reportBadRegionsGenes ;; 5. Visualize results using plotSummary, plotDetailed, and plotSummaryGenes ;; 6. Calculate quantiles using determineQuantiles
workflows.code:
library(BadRegionFinder)
sample_file <- system.file("extdata", "SampleNames2.txt", package = "BadRegionFinder")
samples <- read.table(sample_file)
target_regions <- system.file("extdata", "targetRegions2.bed", package = "BadRegionFinder")
targetRegions <- read.table(target_regions, header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bam_input <- system.file("extdata", package = "BadRegionFinder")
coverage_summary <- determineCoverage(samples, bam_input, targetRegions, "", TRonly = FALSE)
threshold1 <- 20
threshold2 <- 100
percentage1 <- 0.80
percentage2 <- 0.90
coverage_indicators <- determineCoverageQuality(threshold1, threshold2, percentage1, percentage2, coverage_summary)
regionsOfInterest<-data.frame(chr = c(2,2,17), start = c(198266420,198267200,74732940), end = c(198267032,198267800,74733301))
coverage_indicators_2 <- determineRegionsOfInterest(regionsOfInterest, coverage_indicators)
library(biomaRt)
mart = useMart(biomart="ENSEMBL_MART_ENSEMBL",host="https://grch37.ensembl.org", path="/biomart/martservice",dataset="hsapiens_gene_ensembl")
badCoverageSummary <- reportBadRegionsSummary(threshold1, threshold2, percentage1, percentage2, coverage_indicators_2, mart, "")
coverage_indicators_temp <- reportBadRegionsDetailed(threshold1, threshold2, percentage1, percentage2, coverage_indicators_2, "", samples, "")
badCoverageOverview <- reportBadRegionsGenes(threshold1, threshold2, percentage1, percentage2, badCoverageSummary, "")
plotSummary(threshold1, threshold2, percentage1, percentage2, badCoverageSummary, "")
plotDetailed(threshold1, threshold2, percentage1, percentage2, coverage_indicators_temp, "")
plotSummaryGenes(threshold1, threshold2, percentage1, percentage2, badCoverageOverview, "")
quantiles <- c(0.5)
coverage_summary2 <- determineQuantiles(coverage_summary, quantiles, "")
